paragraphs.final_prose: The estimation samples are built in three layers, which is why the number of observations varies from one table to the next. The first layer is the base call panel: every matched Capital IQ call of a US public, non-financial, non-utility firm over 2002 to 2018, excluding CEOs with fewer than five calls, for whom no speaking style and hence no residual can be estimated. The second is the SDC deal universe: US public-acquirer deals over the same period with status completed, pending, or withdrawn and a known payment composition, where deals at least half in cash form the cash arm and deals at least half in stock form the stock placebo arm, each firm's first qualifying deal setting its event clock. subsections.title: Ruling Out Analyst Scrutiny

paragraphs.final_prose: The scrutiny alternative holds that pre-deal quarters draw harder analyst questions about cash, and that the hard questions, not the deal, produce the hedged answers. This confound is genuine rather than a strawman: the incidence of cash scrutiny itself rises in the quarter before a cash acquisition ($\mathrm{HighCashScrutiny}$ $0.0408$, $p<0.05$; Table~\ref{tab:empire_building_did}, column~4), so it co-moves with both the cash position and the event and could in principle generate the run-up mechanically. The continuous volume of cash questions does not rise significantly over the same window ($\mathrm{CashScrutiny}$ $0.0854$, not significant; column~3), so the genuine confound is the incidence of cash scrutiny, not its volume. We therefore put it directly to the data in three steps.

It uses empire_building_did col 4 (the promise/delivery split); the cash-arm result columns stay in 3.2.

paragraphs.final_prose: Step one establishes that the scrutiny measure is real. The share of analyst question-and-answer turns devoted to cash and liquidity rises strongly with the firm's cash ratio ($0.7530$ in a one-tailed test, $p<0.01$; Table~\ref{tab:cash_scrutiny_validity}, column~1, and $0.8519$, $p<0.01$, with the full control set, column~2) and with a high-cash indicator ($0.1754$, $p<0.01$; column~3), so the nulls that follow are not the artifact of a dead measure.

paragraphs.final_prose: Step two shows that scrutiny alone does not move the residual. Its direct effect on $\mathrm{UncResCEO}$ is zero to four decimal places ($-0.0000$, standard error $0.0013$, across $41{,}512$ calls; Table~\ref{tab:cash_scrutiny_channel}, Panel~A), and the null holds under a logit on the dichotomized residual ($-0.0003$; Panel~B) and on the raw uncertainty measure and the coarser scrutiny proxies alike. This null is non-redundant with the residual's construction, because $\mathrm{CashScrutiny}$ is the volume of cash questions, whereas the question-uncertainty wording, $\mathrm{UncQue}$, is already netted out inside the residual by the decomposition of Section~2.3.
